doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

chapter: Meeting Joe and life with the Basie band
title: Meeting Joe Williams in 1957 at the Waldorf and Birdland
summary: She describes a revolving-door first meeting outside the Waldorf Astoria, the night out at Birdland with Marshall Royal, missing him in England, and meeting again months later.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well there’s an old saying that comedians use that they met in a revolving door and they’ve been going ‘round together ever since. But in our case it’s actually true. Of course I was working in New York City and some English friends came to town and wanted to celebrate because they were on their way to the U.K. And so we went out for the evening and we went to see George Shearing, who was at The Embers in those days, and then we went on the Waldorf Astoria, where the Count Basie Orchestra was playing with Sarah Vaughan and Joe Williams. We were already familiar with Joe and the band of course and Sarah. And after the show we were down in the lobby going out onto Park Avenue, and I got out onto the street as Joe was coming back in to the hotel because he’d forgotten his putter, which is all-important to him as you probably know. It’s still his favorite thing. And so you know I was going out and he was coming in and we glanced at each other, and I found myself left out alone on the street, and realized that he was talking to my friends in the lobby, and Marshall Royal was also there, he was in the band at the time. And we all ended up going to Birdland together, which was great fun. And that’s how we initially met. And then later on, Joe came to England, I went back to England and Joe came to England to do a Command Performance. And I tried to contact him, because there was a little something, and I tried to contact him and he was busy or lost my number or something and we missed each other. But then they came back to England later on, a few months later and we met again and we’ve been going out together ever since.
That was not a very tactful question.
Why? I don’t mind. Can’t hide our ages.
